ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a composite figure made up of a left trapezoid and a right semicircle. The upper base of the trapezoid is labeled 22 cm, the lower base is labeled 31 cm, and the left slanted side is labeled 15 cm. The right semicircle is connected to the vertical right side of the trapezoid, and the right-angle markings in the figure show that the upper and lower bases of the trapezoid are perpendicular to this vertical line, so this vertical line is also the diameter of the semicircle. Reasoning: The difference between the lengths of the upper and lower bases of the trapezoid is 31 - 22 = 9 cm, which represents the horizontal leg length of the right triangle formed by the left slanted side, with hypotenuse 15 cm. Use the Pythagorean theorem to find the trapezoid height: h = sqrt(15^2 - 9^2) = sqrt(225 - 81) = sqrt(144) = 12 cm. The diameter of the semicircle equals this height, 12 cm, so the radius r = 6 cm. The area of the trapezoid is ((22 + 31) / 2) * 12 = 318 cm². The area of the semicircle is (1/2)π(6^2) = 18π ≈ 56.5 cm². The total area is 318 + 18π ≈ 374.5 cm².

raw_record.question_text: Find the area of the figure. If necessary, round to the nearest tenth.

method.method_draft: Read the figure as a trapezoid attached to a semicircle on the right. From the image, the top horizontal base of the trapezoid is 22 cm, the bottom horizontal base is 31 cm, and the left slanted side is 15 cm. The horizontal offset between the two trapezoid bases is 31−22=9 cm, so use the right triangle formed by the slanted side to get the height: h=sqrt(15^2−9^2)=12 cm. The semicircle’s diameter is this same vertical height, so its radius is 6 cm. Compute area = trapezoid area + semicircle area = ((22+31)/2)*12 + (1/2)π*6^2, then round to the nearest tenth to obtain 374.5.
